title: Massanutten Rental Watch
about: Short-term rental news for Massanutten owners from public county and association records.

county.name: Rockingham County
county.headline: Work with rental owners, in public
county.lede: Owners are asking the Board of Supervisors to treat short-term rental owners as stakeholders: talk with us, and set rental rules in public meetings with time for comment.

main_action.title: Apply for your county rental permit by December 31: a complete application is what counts
main_action.short: At the November 12 work session, staff said rentals that apply by the deadline would keep operating under the new zoning rules. The deadline is still December 31. A possible extension to April 1 goes to the Board on December 9, so treat December 31 as real.
main_action.detail: Every short-term rental already operating must apply for the county permit by December 31, 2026. The Board's discussion on November 12 made clear that a complete application, including the fee, is what must be in by the deadline, not an approved permit. Staff said homes permitted by the deadline could continue under the draft zoning rules, while new rentals hosting more than 10 guests would need a special use permit and commercial building standards. Whether that status passes to a buyer when a home is sold was not answered.
steps: Download the application from the county's Short-Term Rentals page.
The form allows up to two guests per bedroom, plus four on public sewer. Under the draft, what your permit approves is what continues, so enter the occupancy you actually need, up to that limit.
Attach a site layout, a fire safety and evacuation plan with a diagram for each bedroom, proof of short-term rental liability insurance, and the $200 application fee.
The affidavit of compliance on that page is for renewing next year, not for this application.
Apply now rather than in December. Call the county's short-term rental administrator at (540) 564-3029 to confirm your application is complete, and ask for your approved use and occupancy in writing.

more_actions.title: Before December 1, send the county your questions about the rental zoning rules
more_actions.short: The Board will take up the draft zoning rules again at a work session on Tuesday, December 1. Many basic questions went unanswered on November 12, such as whether a permit's protection passes to a buyer. Owners are gathering them into one courteous list for county staff.
more_actions.detail: On November 12 the Board heard the staff draft but took no position on it. Supervisors said they want time to think and will come back December 1 to give staff direction, and staff said the draft will not change before then. That makes the next two weeks the time for owners' questions to reach the Board and staff.
steps: Add your question to the owners' combined list at the sign-up page. It goes to county staff before December 1.

Good questions are specific: does the permit's protection pass to a buyer, or to an LLC? Can a permitted home renovate or rebuild and keep its occupancy? Which commercial building standards would a new large rental have to meet?
If you write to the Board yourself, keep it short, courteous and in your own words. Massanutten is in District 5, represented by Supervisor Joel Hensley.
Come to the work session if you can: Tuesday, December 1, 3 to 5 PM, at the County Administration Center, 20 East Gay Street, Harrisonburg. The room was full on November 12.

more_actions.title: Get county agendas the moment they are posted
more_actions.short: County agendas post only a few days before each meeting. Free email alerts tell you right away.
more_actions.detail: The county posts Board of Supervisors and Planning Commission agendas only a few days before each meeting. The next Board of Supervisors meeting is Wednesday, October 28 at 6 PM.
steps: Sign up for the county's free email alerts and choose the Agenda Center alerts for the Board of Supervisors and the Planning Commission.
When an agenda includes short-term rentals, speak during public comment or write to your supervisor before the meeting.

coming_up.title: Board work session on the short-term rental zoning rules
coming_up.detail: 3 to 5 PM, before the Planning Commission's 6 PM meeting. The Board will give staff direction on the Chapter 17 zoning draft, including the recreational lodge rule. Location to be confirmed on the county's agenda.

coming_up.title: Board of Supervisors
coming_up.detail: Expected: a Chapter 9 amendment letting the health department's approved septic capacity set occupancy for homes on septic, and possibly an extension of the permit deadline to April 1, 2027.

coming_up.title: Existing short-term rentals must apply for a county permit
coming_up.detail: Set by the ordinance adopted December 10, 2025.

findings.title: Work session: no decisions; the Board returns to the zoning draft December 1
findings.detail: Staff presented the draft zoning, campground and permit changes as a starting point. Supervisors said they want time to think and will give staff direction at a work session on December 1, and staff said the draft will not change before then. The Board directed staff to bring the septic occupancy change to its December 9 meeting.

findings.title: Staff: rentals permitted by the deadline would keep operating under the new zoning
findings.detail: Staff said rentals that obtain the county permit by the deadline would continue, whatever the new zoning says for their district. The recreational lodge rule (special use permit and commercial building standards above 10 guests) would apply to new rentals, new construction and homes converting to rental. Grandfathered homes still must meet septic, building, fire and parking requirements. Whether that status passes to a buyer was not answered. Staff also said the Virginia building code itself does not set the 10-guest line.

findings.title: Draft zoning: new rentals by right only in A-1, A-2, RV and R-4; Massanutten stays by right
findings.detail: Under the draft, new short-term rentals in single-family homes would be allowed by right only in the A-1, A-2, RV and R-4 (Massanutten) districts, need a special use permit in RR-1, and be prohibited in R-1, R-2, R-3 and the planned residential districts. Duplexes and rowhouses would be allowed only in R-4, at two guests per bedroom. Owner-occupied rentals would be allowed everywhere, with a 90-day yearly limit when the owner is away.

findings.title: Permit deadline stays December 31 for now; April 1 extension to be considered December 9
findings.detail: Supervisors split on extending the deadline. As discussion ended, an extension to April 1, 2027 appeared to have enough support to come back for consideration at the December 9 meeting, but no vote was taken. Staff said about 84 permits were approved and 21 were in review as of November 5, out of an estimated 700 or more rentals. A complete application by the deadline is what counts.

findings.title: Draft county zoning rules: over 10 guests would need a special permit and commercial construction
findings.detail: The packet for the November 12 work session proposes adding short-term rentals to the zoning ordinance. A rental with more than 10 guests becomes a "recreational lodge," allowed only by special use permit in the A-1, A-2, RV, RR-1, and R-4 districts and built to commercial code. Homes that already hold the county permit may continue; homes without one by the deadline would need the special use permit and commercial upgrades to host more than 10. Rentals of 10 or fewer stay allowed by right in A-1, A-2, RV, and R-4 (Massanutten's covenants describe its lots as zoned R-4), need a special use permit in RR-1, and are barred in R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-5 neighborhoods unless the owner lives there. A rental may include only one dwelling unit, so no renting a second living space in the same house. Owner-occupied homes can rent without limit while the owner is present and up to 90 days a year when away. Septic homes would be limited to two guests per bedroom unless the health department approves more. The permit deadline is listed as a topic for discussion.

findings.title: Draft came from a Land Use Committee that met in June and September
findings.detail: The work session packet says that after public input and a local court case, the Board formed a Land Use Committee to recommend zoning approaches for short-term rentals, and that it met June 15 and September 10, 2026. Its direction: define short-term rentals, address them in residential neighborhoods, address owner-occupied rental periods, and address rentals over ten guests. A search of the county website finds no notice, agenda, or minutes for those meetings.

findings.title: 84 county rental permits approved, 21 in review
findings.detail: As of November 5, the county had approved 84 short-term rental permits and had 21 more in review, according to the work session packet. Applications opened in June 2026.

findings.title: County fee schedule: $200 rental permit, $250 to appeal
findings.detail: The county's amended fiscal 2027 fee schedule, posted November 3, lists a $200 fee for a short-term rental permit application or renewal and a $250 fee to appeal a violation finding, a revocation, or a refused permit, both effective July 1, 2026.

findings.title: Short-term rental work session set for November 12 at 11 AM
findings.detail: The county's public notice says the Board of Supervisors and the Planning Commission will meet jointly to discuss short-term rentals on Thursday, November 12 at 11 AM in the Community Development Meeting Room, Entrance C, Rockingham County Administration Center, 20 East Gay Street, Harrisonburg. No agenda or materials are posted yet.

findings.title: Board and Planning Commission to hold a joint work session on short-term rentals November 12
findings.detail: The November 4 Planning Commission agenda lists upcoming joint work sessions with the Board of Supervisors: short-term rentals on November 12 and strategic planning on December 3. No time, materials, or agenda for the session are posted yet. Work sessions usually take no public comment, so writing beforehand is the way to be heard.

findings.title: Board denied the 10-bedroom short-term rental barn, 5 to 0
findings.detail: On October 14 the Board denied a permit to turn a barn on Resort Drive, McGaheysville, into a second dwelling with up to 10 bedrooms for short-term rental. Supervisor Hensley, who represents Massanutten, made the motion; he said the application left out maximum occupancy and that second dwellings on farm land were meant for family or farming. Chair Longcor and Supervisor Dale called the rental a commercial business in a non-commercial zone. Neighbors spoke against it. Source: the October 14 minutes in the October 28 agenda packet.

findings.title: Another approval came with a ban on short-term rentals
findings.detail: Also on October 14, the Board approved a second dwelling in Cross Keys for an aging parent, with the condition that neither house may ever be a short-term rental. Supervisor Dale proposed the condition. Supervisor Wolfe-Garrison objected that it limits property rights and sets a precedent, but the vote was 5 to 0.

findings.title: County has approved 26 short-term rental permits so far
findings.detail: The community development report in the October 28 agenda packet lists 26 approved permits. Every short-term rental already operating must apply by December 31.

findings.title: Massanutten water and sewer rates up for review in early December
findings.detail: On October 14 county staff said they have finished the promised one-year review of Massanutten Water and Sewer Authority rates and asked for a work session with the authority in early December. No date is set yet.

findings.title: Board met in closed session on litigation, with the rental administrator present
findings.detail: On October 2 the Board held a 46-minute closed meeting for consultation with legal counsel about actual or probable litigation. The county's Short-Term Rental Administrator, the zoning administrators, and the community development director attended. The minutes do not say what the litigation is.

findings.title: County updated the short-term rental application form
findings.detail: The Short Term Rental Application in the county's document center carries a new date of October 2, 2026. What changed has not been compared yet.

findings.title: Board keeps barring short-term rentals in second dwellings
findings.detail: At the September 23 meeting, applicants for a second-dwelling permit (SUP26-0903) offered a condition prohibiting short-term rentals. On July 8 the Board added the same condition to another approval by a 4 to 1 vote, at Supervisor Wolfe-Garrison's request.

association.name: Massanutten covenants
association.headline: Owners should shape the covenant rewrite
association.lede: The association is rewriting the covenants every owner lives under. No comment deadline or vote process has been posted, so comment now while changes are still possible.

main_action.title: Tell the association what you think of Covenants 1 and 19
main_action.short: Covenant 1 would ban outdoor fires without written approval. Covenant 19 adds new limits on activities, lighting, and quiet hours. Seven more sections were posted October 31, including Covenant 25 on assessments. No deadline is posted.
main_action.detail: The covenant rewrite is open for owner comment and no deadline has been posted. Two changes affect every owner. Covenant 1 would ban all outdoor fires without the association's written approval, which could cover gas fire tables, fire pits, outdoor fireplaces, and grills, and an approval could be revoked at any time. Covenant 19 adds an undefined test that activities, amenities, and lighting be consistent with a single-family home on a comparably sized lot, and lets the association set quiet hours for noise and lighting without an owner vote.
steps: Open the feedback form. Each covenant has its own comment box.

Covenant 1 box: ask that outdoor fire be defined as burning wood, brush, leaves, or trash, and campfires; that gas fire features and grills be expressly allowed; and that an approval be revocable only for cause or during an official burn ban.

Covenant 19 box: ask that the sentence about being consistent with a single-family home be removed, that quiet hours be set only after owner notice and comment, and that entry, path, and stair safety lighting be exempt.

New on October 31: read Covenants 3, 9 and 10, 12, 15, 25, 26, and 29, and use their boxes if they matter to you. Covenant 25 drops the word "reasonable" and the list of purposes from annual assessments; Covenant 9 requires approval to remove most trees.
Use your own words. Short comments from many owners carry more weight than one long letter.
The form asks for your name, Massanutten address, and email.

more_actions.title: Go to the Covenant Amendment Task Force meeting on November 19
more_actions.short: The task force now meets on its own on November 19. It is the next chance to raise Covenants 1 and 19 in person. Time and place are not posted yet.
more_actions.detail: The association's calendar moved the Covenant Amendment Task Force from a shared November 5 meeting with the Rules Committee to its own meeting on Thursday, November 19.
steps: Call the association office at (540) 289-9466 or email Mpoa@MassanuttenVillage.com to ask the time and place and whether owners may speak.
If owners may speak, keep comments to about three minutes and stick to Covenants 1 and 19.

coming_up.title: Covenant Amendment Task Force
coming_up.detail: Moved here from November 5, where it had shared a meeting with the Rules Committee. Time and place not listed.

coming_up.title: Association Board of Directors
coming_up.detail: Saturday. Time and place not listed.

coming_up.title: Rules Committee
coming_up.detail: The calendar no longer lists the covenant task force for this date.

coming_up.title: Firewise meeting
coming_up.detail: Wildfire safety group; relevant to Covenant 1.

findings.title: Seven more covenant sections posted for comment, including assessments
findings.detail: The proposed changes page was rebuilt with Covenants 3, 9 and 10, 12, 15, 25, 26, and 29 posted for the first time. Covenant 25 would let the association set annual assessments without the original's word "reasonable" or its list of purposes. Covenant 9 requires approval to remove any tree over six feet tall or six inches thick, with possible replacement or monetary restitution. Covenant 3 drops the promise that approvals will not be unreasonable. Covenant 15 limits overnight parking of heavy vehicles. Covenant 26 has no text yet. The proposals for Covenants 1, 19, and 28 are unchanged.

findings.title: Covenant task force meeting moved to November 19
findings.detail: The association's calendar now lists November 5 and December 3 as Rules Committee meetings only, and gives the Covenant Amendment Task Force its own meeting on Thursday, November 19. No time or place is listed.
